title: GPU Financing Filters Into ABS With Stonebriar, Wingspire Deals
source_used: TokenPost (own article on the two deals, read in full). Bloomberg original not opened (HTTP 403); MarketScreener, Finimize, Traders Union and Crypto Briefing blocked.
key_facts: Wingspire Equipment Finance and Stonebriar Commercial Finance are bringing equipment-contract payments to bond investors through separate securitizations.
Wingspire's WEF 2026-1 issues six classes of notes totalling $407.07 million; the pool is worth about $438.18 million across 211 contracts and 63 borrowers, with a yield of about 9.22%.

Stonebriar's SCF 2026-1, its 15th equipment-backed securities deal, has a pool with an initial discounted contract balance of about $957.87 million across 96 contracts and 47 borrowers, weighted average internal rate of return 9.65%.
Stonebriar's collateral covers marine, mining, real estate, energy and manufacturing equipment and certain vehicle leases; its public summary does not specify an AI-related share.
Wingspire separately announced $140 million of equipment financing on 20 Aug 2026 for high-density GPU servers for a private-equity-backed cloud provider; it is not established as part of WEF 2026-1.
Neither public summary specifies how much collateral is tied to AI computing.
Bloomberg's headline (text not opened): 'GPU Financing Filters Into ABS With Stonebriar, Wingspire Deals'.
quote_evidence: Wingspire Equipment Finance and Stonebriar Commercial Finance are bringing equipment contract payments to bond investors through separate securitizations, though their public summaries do not specify how much collateral is tied to AI computing.
The public transaction summary does not specify an AI-related share.

Wingspire separately announced $140 million in equipment financing on Aug. 20, 2026, for high-density GPU servers for a private equity-backed cloud provider serving AI labs, businesses and public-sector organizations.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-chip loans may be reaching the bond market, but the public deal summaries do not show how much of the collateral is AI-related.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (HTTP 403); other outlets on the deals were blocked or only repeat the headline.
